reference_opening.argument: This video is scam content because it presents BitClub membership and mining-pool participation as an earning opportunity, with an invitation to join, an activation fee, and an instructional Bitcoin payment flow. It claims that buying mining shares produces daily payouts lasting 1000 or 2000 days while showing a wallet amount entered for payment, although the available video evidence does not establish that payment was completed or that payouts occurred.

citations.quote: When you join the mining pool, a $99 activation fee will be charged
Once connected to the pool, you have mining with a daily payout for 1000 or 2000 days
This is where you put in the new member's personal information after the enrollment process, the new member can login to their own Bitclub account they need to verify their account
Once the membership is paid and activated, the member can be placed in the binary structure by the sponsor

opening.argument: Judge the precision of the claim being made. The narration says participation in a mining pool can be profitable; it does not promise that a buyer will earn a specified profit. It also says activation can take time and that connection to the physical pool takes 30 days. Those qualifications matter: the video describes a process and an expected payout schedule, not proof that any particular viewer will receive a return. The stated daily payouts should be read as the platform's described operation, not as a verified outcome or an unconditional earnings guarantee.

citations.quote: To be part of a mining pool can be very profitable and is a relatively easy process via Bitclub network.
When your mining pool is paid, it may take between two to 24 hours before it gets activated.
Please note that it takes 30 days before your pool is connected to the physical mining pool.
Once connected to the pool, you have mining with a daily payout for 1000 or 2000 days

rebuttal.rebuttal: The opening correctly identifies the fee and payout statement, but neither establishes a guaranteed profit or an actual payout. It also acknowledges that the available evidence does not show payment completed. An account-verification step and a sponsor's placement of a member describe the proposed workflow; by themselves, they do not establish what any participant ultimately received.

citations.quote: When you join the mining pool, a $99 activation fee will be charged
Once the membership is paid and activated, the member can be placed in the binary structure by the sponsor

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The delays are operational conditions, not risk warnings. The video says joining requires a $99 activation fee, then instructs viewers to buy mining shares and describes daily payouts lasting 1000 or 2000 days. Whether a payment or payout was completed on screen does not change the paid-participation-for-returns proposition being presented.

citations.quote: When you join the mining pool, a $99 activation fee will be charged
Once the membership is activated, you go to buy mining shares.
Once connected to the pool, you have mining with a daily payout for 1000 or 2000 days

opening.argument: This is organized as a walkthrough of account operations. It begins by explaining two ways to obtain cryptocurrency, then moves through member enrollment, email verification, copying a payment address into a wallet, and placing a member in the account's team interface. The title likewise describes how to upgrade an account and buy a pool. A judge can recognize that the demonstrated service makes claims about payouts without treating every explanation of its interface as a claim that the narrator has verified those payouts. The evidence shows an instructional sequence, not a completed earnings result.

citations.quote: There are two different ways to get hold of cryptocurrency.
go to the registered e-mail and copy the code that has been sent.
Copy the address in your BitClub account and go to your Bitcoin wallet .
how to upgrade your account and buy pool in Bitclub Network
Then click on Add member and confirm the location. Now the member is successfully placed.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The reference opening treats instruction as solicitation. But its own cited enrollment and team-placement steps are exactly the sort of interface actions a tutorial explains. The wallet sequence shows how the proposed payment would be entered; it does not show that the narrator received mining proceeds or independently vouched for them. The payout sentence is a claim described during that walkthrough, not evidence of an observed payout.

citations.quote: An existing member can create a link to a new account via the button, enroll member.
Click Send Money and paste the address
Once connected to the pool, you have mining with a daily payout for 1000 or 2000 days

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The instructional format is part of what makes this consequential. The walkthrough does not merely explain mining in general: it directs account upgrade, Bitcoin payment, and purchase of mining shares, then presents daily payouts as the result of joining the pool. No completed payout is needed to identify the paid mining-returns pitch conveyed by those instructions.

citations.quote: When you join the mining pool, a $99 activation fee will be charged you can only pay this fee in bitcoins
Once the membership is activated, you go to buy mining shares.
Once connected to the pool, you have mining with a daily payout for 1000 or 2000 days

opening.argument: The transaction is presented as a purchase of access to a mining service: an activation fee, a choice among packages with different benefits, and a wallet payment procedure. The sponsor can later position the member in a team structure, but the cited placement instructions do not say that recruits generate income for that sponsor. Nor does the payout statement specify a profit amount or show one being paid. Those limits matter when deciding whether this evidence establishes a deceptive scheme, as opposed to a service describing its purchase and account-management process. This reading does not certify the service; it keeps the conclusion tied to what the video actually shows.

citations.quote: When you join the mining pool, a $99 activation fee will be charged
Here you can choose from six different packages with different benefits.
Once the membership is paid and activated, the member can be placed in the binary structure by the sponsor.
Once connected to the pool, you have mining with a daily payout for 1000 or 2000 days

rebuttal.rebuttal: A fee, wallet instructions, and binary placement warrant scrutiny, but the reference opening does not cite a promised sponsor commission or a completed return. The account-verification language concerns access to the member's own account. On this record, the narrower reading is a walkthrough of a paid service and its stated terms, without treating the service's claims as proven true.

citations.quote: the new member can login to their own Bitclub account they need to verify their account
Once the membership is paid and activated, the member can be placed in the binary structure by the sponsor

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The absence of a stated sponsor commission does not answer the central issue. The video instructs a viewer to pay an activation fee in Bitcoin, buy mining shares, and expect daily payouts after connection to the pool. Calling the packages a service does not remove the direct link the narration makes between paying for mining participation and receiving recurring returns.
